chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When one of you has a deceased person, shroud him facing the Qiblah; and similarly, when he is washed, a place for the washing is dug for him facing the Qiblah, so that he faces it with the soles of his feet and his face towards the Qiblah.
ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person be positioned during shrouding and washing according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific orientation of the deceased during ghusl and kafan, ensuring the body faces the Qiblah to maintain spiritual alignment with God until burial. Shia scholars emphasize this practice as a continuation of the Sunnah, reflecting the deceased's eternal orientation toward the Kaaba. The instruction to dig a specific spot for washing highlights the ritual purity and care taken in preparing the body for its final journey.
